messages:
alex: Heads-up — after the FP8 calibration patch merged this morning we're seeing a 12-18% tail latency bump on multi-turn chat workloads. Noticed across both dedicated and hosted lanes. :frowning:
maya: Ugh. Is this the calibration that adjusted scale factors per-layer?
devon: Yes, that one. I ran a quick per-token profile on a repro trace. Raw numbers look like matmul kernel time increased and KV eviction jitter spiked.
li: Can you paste the per-token breakdown? Even ballpark helps.
alex: Sure — snippet from `rdw-perf trace --id xx123`:
```
# per-token latency (ms)
token 45: aten_matmul_fp8 1.32, attention_kv_lookup 0.18, sync 0.42, total 1.92
token 46: aten_matmul_fp8 1.40, attention_kv_lookup 0.25, sync 0.40, total 2.05
token 47: aten_matmul_fp8 1.35, attention_kv_lookup 0.19, sync 0.41, total 1.95
```
maya: matmul increase ~0.15ms avg. That matches a kernel fallback to a slower path? Kernel counters?
devon: Pulled kernel counters from the same run:
```
FP8_KERNEL_INVOCATIONS: 1_234_102
FP8_MATMUL_SLOWPATH: 41
INT8_MATMUL_INVOC: 0
KV_CACHE_EVICTIONS: 82
KV_CACHE_HITS: 3_210
BATCHER_QUEUE_LEN_P90: 7
```
devon: Those 41 slowpath invocations correlate with sequences where quant calibration changed per-layer scale mid-request — we end up reselecting kernels.
ryan: Could be batching heuristics too. If a request initially uses the fast path and later gets different sequence lengths, the runtime might repartition batches and trigger a different codegen.
li: How often are we recalibrating at runtime? I thought calibrate was offline, but the patch enabled a light-weight runtime adapt step.
maya: Yep the new behavior recomputes a tiny per-layer rescale on the first few tokens for long-lived sessions. It was meant to improve quality but may cause kernel selection churn.
alex: I also saw KV cache latency variance when evictions happen near a batch boundary. Example log: `kv_cache: eviction(82) took 3.1ms` for some tokens. That's adding to tail.
devon: Repro recipe I used: 1) model=redwood-xl-13b-quant-fp8, 2) warm-up with 8 tokens, 3) long chat + random context inserts. The regression shows up reliably.
ryan: Can we toggle the runtime adapt step as a flag and run A/B to measure quality vs perf?
maya: Good idea. I ran a quick AB locally: toggle off -> tail latency down ~14%, but small quality delta on eval set (ROUGE/acc down ~0.3%).
li: We need better observability before rolling anything back. Suggestions: expose kernel selection events in traces, add a per-request kernel_variant vector, and emit batching boundary markers.
devon: Agreed. I sketched a lightweight schema for a kernel_event log line: `kernel_event: token_idx, chosen_kernel, reason, matsize, fallback_flag`.
alex: Sample event stream from the failing trace:
```
kernel_event t45: FP8_MATMUL_fast, reason=scale_ok
kernel_event t46: FP8_MATMUL_slowpath, reason=scale_rescale_trigger
kernel_event t47: FP8_MATMUL_fast, reason=scale_ok
```
ryan: That intermittent slowpath explains spikes. Also check thread-local memory thrash when we do rescale — some syncs happen currently.
maya: Action items: 1) add kernel_event to traces (devon doing), 2) add metric `kernel_slowpath_ratio` per-model/route (li), 3) add toggle flag to disable runtime rescale for Dedicated while we debug (alex).
devon: I'll open a small PR that instruments the kernel selector and adds the event lines and a prom counter.
li: I'll add dashboards: per-token latency heatmap, `kernel_slowpath_ratio`, `kv_eviction_rate`, and correlate with `batcher_queue_len_p90`.
ryan: For triage — roll back the runtime adapt toggle for hosted for now? Or just disable it on high-p99 routes.
alex: Rolling back globally would hide potential quality gains. Propose we disable for high-concurrency routes and run AB on low-concurrency first.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: rollback flag toggled -> `runtime.adaptive_rescale=false` on cluster:dedicated-us-west (by alex)
maya: After toggling off on dedicated, initial quick smoke shows p99 dropping back to baseline. Need more samples.
devon: I'll attach the synthetic trace and kernel_event dump to the issue. Also exploring whether small epsilon change in rescale thresholds prevents kernel switch.
li: Nice. If we can avoid kernel-switch churn we should keep the quality path. Maybe only trigger runtime rescale if stable for N consecutive tokens.
ryan: Sounds good. Keep me posted — I'll own the rollout policy change in console to make targeted disables easier.
alex: Thanks all. Will track in the perf-quant ticket. :thumbsup:
